verses.1: Samson went down to Timnah and saw a woman there, one of the daughters of the Philistines.
verses.2: He went up and told his father and mother, "I have seen a woman in Timnah, one of the daughters of the Philistines. Now please get her for me as my wife."
verses.3: His father and mother said to him, "Is there no woman among the daughters of your relatives or among all our people that you must go to take a wife from the uncircumcised Philistines?"
verses.4: But Samson said to his father, "Please get her for me, for she is pleasing to my eyes." His father and mother did not know that it was the LORD who was seeking an opportunity to confront the Philistines, for at that time the Philistines ruled over Israel.
verses.5: Samson went down with his father and mother to Timnah, and when they reached the vineyards of Timnah, suddenly a young lion roared at him.
verses.6: The Spirit of the LORD came upon him in power, and he tore the lion apart as one might tear a kid. He did this without holding anything in his hands. He did not tell his father or mother what he had done.
verses.7: He went down and spoke to the woman, and she pleased him.
verses.8: After some days, he went back to take her, and as he turned aside, he saw the carcass of the lion, and there was a swarm of bees and honey in the lion's body.
verses.9: He scraped the honey into his hands and went on, eating as he went. Then he gave some to his father and mother, and they ate it, but he did not tell them that the honey had come from the body of the lion.
verses.10: His father went down to the woman, and there Samson held a feast, for the young men used to do this.
verses.11: When they saw him, they took thirty companions and went with him.
verses.12: Samson said to them, "Let me give you a riddle. If you can solve it in the seven days of the feast and discover it, I will give you thirty linen garments and thirty sets of clothing.
verses.13: But if you cannot solve it, you must give me thirty linen garments and thirty sets of clothing." They said to him, "Give us your riddle, and we will listen to it."
verses.14: He said to them, "From the eater comes food, and from the strong comes sweetness." For three days they could not solve the riddle.
verses.15: On the seventh day, they said to Samson's wife, "Coax your husband to tell us the riddle, or we will burn you and your father's house with fire. Did you not invite us? Is that not why you called us in?"
verses.16: So Samson's wife wept over him and said, "You only hate me and do not love me. You have given your riddle to the men of my people and have not told me." Samson said to her, "I did not tell my father or mother, and I will not tell you."
verses.17: For seven days her weeping continued, as long as their feast lasted. On the seventh day, moved by her tears, he told her the riddle, and she passed it on to the men of her people.
verses.18: The men of the city said to him on the seventh day, before the sun had risen, "What is sweeter than honey? What is stronger than a lion?" Then he said to them, "If you had not plowed with my heifer, you would not have discovered my riddle."
verses.19: The Spirit of the LORD came upon him, and he went down to Ashkelon. He struck down thirty men of the city, took their garments, and gave the clothing to those who had explained the riddle. Then his anger flared, and he went up to his father's house.
verses.20: Samson's wife was given to one of his companions.

notes:
Notes
- v. 14: "From the eater comes food, and from the strong comes sweetness" — the riddle plays on the dual meanings of "eater" (lion) and "strong" (lion), with the answer being "honey from the lion's carcass."
- v. 18: "If you had not plowed with my heifer..." — the answer to the riddle implies that the men of the city solved it through deception, not wisdom, as they forced Samson's wife to betray him.
raw:
[1] Samson went down to Timnah and saw a woman there, one of the daughters of the Philistines.

[2] He went up and told his father and mother, "I have seen a woman in Timnah, one of the daughters of the Philistines. Now please get her for me as my wife."

[3] His father and mother said to him, "Is there no woman among the daughters of your relatives or among all our people that you must go to take a wife from the uncircumcised Philistines?"

[4] But Samson said to his father, "Please get her for me, for she is pleasing to my eyes." His father and mother did not know that it was the LORD who was seeking an opportunity to confront the Philistines, for at that time the Philistines ruled over Israel.

[5] Samson went down with his father and mother to Timnah, and when they reached the vineyards of Timnah, suddenly a young lion roared at him.

[6] The Spirit of the LORD came upon him in power, and he tore the lion apart as one might tear a kid. He did this without holding anything in his hands. He did not tell his father or mother what he had done.

[7] He went down and spoke to the woman, and she pleased him.

[8] After some days, he went back to take her, and as he turned aside, he saw the carcass of the lion, and there was a swarm of bees and honey in the lion's body.

[9] He scraped the honey into his hands and went on, eating as he went. Then he gave some to his father and mother, and they ate it, but he did not tell them that the honey had come from the body of the lion.

[10] His father went down to the woman, and there Samson held a feast, for the young men used to do this.

[11] When they saw him, they took thirty companions and went with him.

[12] Samson said to them, "Let me give you a riddle. If you can solve it in the seven days of the feast and discover it, I will give you thirty linen garments and thirty sets of clothing.

[13] But if you cannot solve it, you must give me thirty linen garments and thirty sets of clothing." They said to him, "Give us your riddle, and we will listen to it."

[14] He said to them, "From the eater comes food, and from the strong comes sweetness." For three days they could not solve the riddle.

[15] On the seventh day, they said to Samson's wife, "Coax your husband to tell us the riddle, or we will burn you and your father's house with fire. Did you not invite us? Is that not why you called us in?"

[16] So Samson's wife wept over him and said, "You only hate me and do not love me. You have given your riddle to the men of my people and have not told me." Samson said to her, "I did not tell my father or mother, and I will not tell you."

[17] For seven days her weeping continued, as long as their feast lasted. On the seventh day, moved by her tears, he told her the riddle, and she passed it on to the men of her people.

[18] The men of the city said to him on the seventh day, before the sun had risen, "What is sweeter than honey? What is stronger than a lion?" Then he said to them, "If you had not plowed with my heifer, you would not have discovered my riddle."

[19] The Spirit of the LORD came upon him, and he went down to Ashkelon. He struck down thirty men of the city, took their garments, and gave the clothing to those who had explained the riddle. Then his anger flared, and he went up to his father's house.

[20] Samson's wife was given to one of his companions.

---
Notes
- v. 14: "From the eater comes food, and from the strong comes sweetness" — the riddle plays on the dual meanings of "eater" (lion) and "strong" (lion), with the answer being "honey from the lion's carcass."
- v. 18: "If you had not plowed with my heifer..." — the answer to the riddle implies that the men of the city solved it through deception, not wisdom, as they forced Samson's wife to betray him.
